verdict: Salesforce grew revenue 11% to $8.72B and turned its cost-cutting year into real profit — net income jumped to $1.22B from $210M a year ago, with a 17.2% GAAP operating margin.

segments.name: Subscription and support
segments.note: The core software subscriptions — Sales, Service, Slack, Marketing and Commerce clouds, MuleSoft and Tableau.

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Consulting and training that help big customers roll the software out — a shrinking sideline whose direct costs ($584M) again exceeded its revenue.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform — including the Einstein AI push — down 6% YoY after the restructuring.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: The largest running cost — Salesforce's big sales force and marketing machine, down 5% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — down 5% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: Severance and office-exit charges from the January 2023 restructuring plan.

takeaways.title: The margin plan worked
takeaways.text: GAAP operating margin reached 17.2%, up from 5.9% a year ago, as the January 2023 restructuring cut spending — research, sales and admin costs all fell in dollar terms even as revenue grew 11%.

takeaways.title: Cash poured in
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $1.53B, up 389% year-over-year, and free cash flow was $1.37B — the profit is turning into cash, not just accounting gains.

takeaways.title: The order book kept growing
takeaways.text: Current remaining performance obligation — work customers have contracted for but Salesforce has not yet billed as revenue — reached $23.9B, up 14% year-over-year.

oneTimers: $55M of restructuring charges in the quarter from the January 2023 plan (workforce cuts and office exits); $815M was booked across the first nine months of FY24.
A $72M mark-down on strategic investments — stakes Salesforce holds in other companies — which cut GAAP EPS by about $0.06.
otherDetail: A $72M loss on strategic investments (stakes Salesforce holds in other companies), partly offset by $58M of other income — mostly interest earned, net of interest on Salesforce's debt: a net -$14M.
